headline: Strong US growth and steady inflation figures kept a December Federal Reserve hike likely, yet the dollar ended slightly lower. The euro recovered after European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said a hike was discussed.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: US growth beat forecasts and the Fed's preferred inflation gauge rose, which lifted bets on a December Federal Reserve hike to about 83%. The dollar still ended slightly lower, as Treasury yields eased and the euro recovered.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Since the US–Iran war began in February, high oil has kept US inflation well above the Federal Reserve's 2% goal, and the Fed raised rates in September. On Wednesday it held its range at 3.75–4.00%, with two officials voting for a hike, while chair Kevin Warsh refused to commit to December. What changed: The US economy grew at a 3.4% yearly pace in July to September, above the 3.2% expected. The Fed's preferred price gauge, PCE, rose to 3.6% a year from 3.4%, mostly on gasoline; leaving out food and energy it rose 0.3% on the month, as forecast, or 3.1% a year. Weekly jobless claims stayed near 57-year lows. Bets on a December hike rose to about 83% from about 78% in the morning, but the dollar index slipped about 0.2% to near 102.15 as the 10-year Treasury yield eased below 5%. What it means: The figures gave the Fed no reason to back away from a hike, but nothing hot enough to force it either; core prices did what was expected. With a hike already mostly priced, the dollar needs a fresh surprise to climb. The question to keep asking: does any figure before December 9 make a hike unavoidable, or give the Fed a reason to wait?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the US Employment Cost Index, a key wage gauge, at 7:30 AM CT Friday, then Fed officials Mary Daly and Alberto Musalem at about 11:00 AM CT. October jobs figures follow next week; the next Fed decision is December 9.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The European Central Bank held its deposit rate at 2.50%, and the euro first fell to its weakest since May 2025, near $1.111. It recovered to about $1.116 after President Christine Lagarde said a hike had been discussed, pointing to December.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Energy costs from the Iran war have pushed euro-area inflation to about 3.8%, and the European Central Bank raised its deposit rate twice this year, to 2.50%. France's budget fight has kept a weight on the euro. What changed: The bank held as expected and promised nothing for December, and the euro dipped to about $1.111. At her press conference, Lagarde said a rise had been debated and the direction is clear, and that the bank has tools to calm disorderly selling of French bonds. Markets now see a December 17 hike as very likely, and the euro ended up slightly, near $1.116. Lagarde also announced she will step down on February 7, 2027, about nine months early. A euro-area business and consumer sentiment survey missed forecasts. What it means: The pause looks like a short wait rather than the end of rate rises, which supports the euro. But slowing growth and France's troubles kept the bounce small, and the euro is still near its lowest in 17 months. Her early exit did not change the policy outlook. The question to keep asking: does euro-area inflation stay hot enough to lock in December?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up Friday: euro-area growth for July to September and October inflation flash estimates at 5:00 AM CT, with German inflation at 8:00 AM CT. France's parliament votes on the revenue part of its budget on November 3.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound rose about 0.3% to near $1.3365 and reached its strongest against the euro since May 2025. Softer UK lending figures did not shake expectations of a Bank of England hike on November 5.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September, and markets see a Bank of England hike on November 5 as almost certain. Chancellor John Healey's first Budget on Wednesday passed calmly. What changed: Bank of England figures showed mortgage approvals slipping to about 53,400 in September and consumer borrowing slowing, a sign higher rates are cooling credit. Markets looked past it: the pound gained against a softer US dollar, and the euro slid to about 83.5 pence. What it means: With the Budget out of the way, the pound is trading on rates, and a near-certain UK hike next week keeps it among the strongest major currencies. Cooling credit matters more for how far the Bank goes after November than for the November move itself. The question to keep asking: does the Bank of England hint at a second hike in December?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Nationwide house prices at 2:00 AM CT Friday and US wage figures at 7:30 AM CT, then the Bank of England decision at 6:00 AM CT on November 5 (US clocks change on November 1).

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The dollar ended almost flat near ¥158, after briefly topping that level on the strong US figures. Tokyo inflation figures come at 6:30 PM CT tonight, then the Bank of Japan decides overnight.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Japanese rates are far below US rates, which has kept the yen weak, and Tokyo has warned it is ready to act in the currency market. The Bank of Japan is expected to hold on Friday and raise rates in December. What changed: The dollar touched about ¥158.1 after the US growth beat, then settled near ¥157.97, up less than 0.1%. Easing US Treasury yields kept it from going further. Earlier, Japanese consumer confidence slipped slightly. What it means: The yen is waiting on its own central bank. Firm Tokyo prices and a clear hint toward December from Governor Kazuo Ueda would narrow the rate gap that keeps the yen weak; a vague message would leave the dollar pressing near ¥158, where Tokyo's warnings tend to get louder. The question to keep asking: how soon does the Bank of Japan raise rates again?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Tokyo consumer prices for October, jobs and industrial output at 6:30–6:50 PM CT tonight (core prices forecast 2.6%), then the Bank of Japan decision, new forecasts and Ueda's press conference overnight Thursday CT.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc firmed about 0.2% to near 0.826 per dollar as the dollar softened broadly. There was no Swiss news to move it.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Swiss inflation is below target and the Swiss National Bank holds its rate at zero, so the franc mostly moves as a safe place for money in tense times. The bank has said it is less ready to fight a weaker franc. What changed: The franc edged up to about 0.826 per dollar, in line with a softer dollar against most major currencies. Oil eased and Middle East tension did not flare, so there was no rush for safety. What it means: With no rate move in sight, the franc follows the dollar and the global mood: a flare-up with Iran would lift it, steady calm would keep it soft. The question to keep asking: are investors looking for safety?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the KOF economic barometer at 3:00 AM CT Friday and US wage figures at 7:30 AM CT. The next Swiss rate decision is December 10.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Aussie eased to about 70.3 US cents, off its five-week high near 70.5 in Asia. Markets still expect the Reserve Bank of Australia to raise rates on November 3; producer prices come tonight.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Australian inflation has run above the Reserve Bank of Australia's forecasts, and the bank has raised rates four times this year. Hot inflation figures on Wednesday made a fifth hike, on November 3, likely. What changed: Cheaper import prices, reported overnight, and the strong US figures took a little off the Aussie, which slipped from about 70.5 cents in Asia to 70.3 by the New York close. Nothing changed the case for a November hike. What it means: The Aussie is still supported by one of the most likely rate rises among major banks. Producer prices tonight are the last inflation check before the decision; a firm reading would back the hike, a soft one would add to the sense that price pressure is easing. The question to keep asking: does anything talk the Reserve Bank of Australia out of November?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Australian producer prices and private credit at 7:30 PM CT tonight, China's official factory surveys at 8:30 PM CT Friday, then the Reserve Bank of Australia decision at 9:30 PM CT Monday, November 2.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie held just under 1.40 per US dollar, near 1.3995, and the euro fell to a 15-month low against it. Bank of Canada deputy governor Nicolas Vincent gave no new rate signal; Canada's August growth figures come Friday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Higher energy prices pushed Canadian inflation up, and on Wednesday the Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.50%, its first hike since 2023. Governor Tiff Macklem said more hikes are possible but the bank will proceed carefully. What changed: The loonie gave back a little of its overnight gain, ending near 1.3995 per US dollar, as oil slipped. It kept rising against the euro, which fell to about 1.557 loonies, its weakest in 15 months. Vincent's remarks at a lecture carried no fresh hint on December. What it means: Canada's turn to hikes narrows the rate gap with the US and keeps the loonie firm, even with oil a little lower. Markets give a December hike roughly even odds, so Friday's growth figures matter. The question to keep asking: does Canadian data give the bank reason to hike again in December?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Canada's August GDP and US wage figures, both at 7:30 AM CT Friday. The next Bank of Canada decision is December 9.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi eased slightly to about 56.1 US cents as the strong US figures kept the US dollar supported against smaller currencies. It is still recovering from the central bank's surprise hold on Wednesday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: On Wednesday the Reserve Bank of New Zealand held its rate at 2.75% in a 4–3 vote when almost everyone expected a hike, and the kiwi fell sharply. The bank said more tightening is likely. What changed: Little. A business survey overnight showed confidence rising and firms planning bigger price increases, but the kiwi slipped from about 56.25 cents in Asia to 56.1 by the New York close. What it means: Firmer price plans back a December hike, so the hold looks like a delay rather than a change of mind, which limits the kiwi's downside. Until then it mostly follows the US dollar and the global mood. The question to keep asking: does the December hike look more certain?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US wage figures at 7:30 AM CT Friday and China's factory surveys at 8:30 PM CT Friday. New Zealand job figures come next week; the next Reserve Bank of New Zealand decision is December 9.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Oil fell more than 1%, with Brent near $114 and US crude near $101, as a report that US Vice President JD Vance reached out to Iran kept hopes for talks alive. A ship fire off Oman was not confirmed as an attack.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The US–Iran war, which began in February, disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and has kept oil above $100. Talk of renewed US strikes after next week's midterm elections pushed prices back up earlier this week. What changed: Brent fell about 1.3% to near $113.8 and US crude about 1.6% to near $101.1. The Wall Street Journal's report that Vance wrote to a senior Iranian official kept peace hopes alive, though President Donald Trump denied ordering talks. A merchant ship caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz overnight; UK maritime officials said the cause is under investigation and not a confirmed attack. US natural gas stocks also rose more than expected. What it means: Oil is pulled between hopes for a deal and fear of more fighting, so headlines move it more than supply data. A cheaper barrel helps importers like Japan and the euro area and takes a little support from exporters like Canada. The question to keep asking: are talks with Iran real enough to take the war premium out?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: any reply from Iran to the Vance letter, the OPEC+ meeting on Sunday, expected to keep December output targets unchanged, and the US midterm elections on Tuesday, November 3.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold fell about 1% to near $4,025 an ounce after strong US growth figures kept a December Fed hike likely. It is heading for a second monthly fall.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Gold soared earlier in the Iran war but has struggled since the Fed resumed raising rates, because higher yields make a metal that pays nothing less attractive. What changed: Gold dropped about $45 in the hour after the US growth and inflation figures, as bets on a December Fed hike rose to about 83%. By late morning it was holding near $4,025–4,030 as Treasury yields eased. What it means: Gold is trading as a rates story: every sign the Fed will hike weighs on it, while central-bank buying and the risk of a flare-up with Iran give it a floor near $4,000. The question to keep asking: are US yields still rising?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: euro-area inflation at 5:00 AM CT Friday, US wage figures at 7:30 AM CT and Fed speakers Mary Daly and Alberto Musalem at about 11:00 AM CT.

calls.text: US 10-year yield below 5% after the tech sell-off: if Asian and European stocks keep falling overnight, the yen pushes toward ¥156 and the dollar index slips under 101.5; a rebound in stocks lifts yields and the dollar back toward ¥157.5
calls.note: Asian stocks kept falling (Nikkei −1.3%) and the dollar dipped to about ¥156.3, but steadied near ¥156.9 by 12:40 AM CT; the dollar index held at about 101.5 rather than slipping under it.

calls.text: Euro-area flash business surveys Fri 3:00 AM CT (manufacturing ~52.7, services ~52.6 expected), hours before Moody's on France: misses keep the euro near $1.12; beats firm December ECB hike bets and lift it
calls.note: The surveys missed (euro-area composite 51.9, France back in contraction at 48.4), and the euro stayed near $1.12.

calls.text: US flash PMIs Fri 8:45 AM CT (services ~58.0 expected) and Michigan inflation expectations 9:00 AM CT: firm readings lift yields back toward 5% and steady the dollar; soft ones extend the bond rally
calls.note: The surveys were firm on prices and the Michigan inflation outlook ticked up; the 10-year yield rose back to about 5.00% and the dollar index firmed to about 101.8 on Friday.

calls.text: SNB policy summary 2:30 AM CT: worry about a strong franc keeps December cut bets alive and caps the franc; a calmer tone lets it firm
calls.note: Calmer tone: the bank dropped its stronger readiness to intervene and gave no December cut signal. The franc firmed slightly, with the dollar near 0.823, and hit a three-month high against the euro.

calls.text: Saudi departure order: widening across the Gulf or a hit on Saudi output puts Brent well above $110 and lifts the dollar and loonie; staying contained lets oil drift
calls.note: Brent did climb well above $110 (about $113 by the close), but on reports of US–Israeli strike plans and Iranian tanker claims, not a wider departure order. The loonie edged up; the dollar slipped.

calls.text: UK retail sales Fri 1:00 AM CT (−0.2% expected): a strong print lifts December hike bets and the pound; a weak one trims both
calls.note: Sales fell 0.4%, worse than expected, yet the pound reached its strongest against the euro since May 2025 on Friday as a November Bank of England hike stayed near certain.

calls.text: US jobless claims Thu 7:30 AM CT (about 200,000 expected): staying low keeps the Fed's December hike near 90%; a jump trims it and weighs on the dollar
calls.note: Claims stayed low at 194,000 (200,000 expected), near their lowest in decades. December hike bets held near 90% (CME FedWatch, Oct 21); a sharp bond rally later still pulled the dollar lower.

calls.text: Moody's review of France Fri: a downgrade widens France's gap over German yields and weighs on the euro; holding the rating eases the pressure
calls.note: Moody's held France at Aa3; French yields eased on Monday and the euro led the majors in the European morning.

calls.text: Bailey 8:00 AM CT after the 3.5% UK inflation print: backing November without promising more keeps the pound near $1.34; any opening to a December follow-up lifts it; calling energy temporary trims it
calls.note: Neither branch: Bailey gave no new signal on rates. The pound still held near $1.34 (about 1.3395 at the New York close), with December's second hike about a coin toss.

calls.text: US crude oil stocks 9:30 AM CT (industry survey: about −4.9M barrels): a big official draw keeps Brent above $110; a build lets the rebound fade
calls.note: The draw came (−3.1M barrels, far more than forecast) and Brent briefly topped $110.8, but it still faded to $108.82 at the settle after the US Treasury's tanker licence and emergency fuel loans.

calls.text: Pakistan's mediation after Iran's uranium refusal: any confirmed opening drains oil's premium and lifts the euro and yen; more warships and no talks keep Brent near $110 into the close
calls.note: No opening: Rubio called a deal extremely difficult and more US warships headed in. Brent settled at $108.82, near $110 but off its high on Washington's supply moves rather than diplomacy.

calls.text: Japan national CPI Thu 6:30 PM CT (2.1% expected): a hot print keeps the BoJ's December hike near three in four; a soft one fades it and weighs on the yen
calls.note: Neither branch: 2.1% exactly as expected (1.7% prior), though the measure that also leaves out energy jumped to 2.4%. December hike pricing held near 80%.

calls.text: US–Iran framework: confirmation by either government drains oil's risk premium and pulls US long yields lower; another denial puts Brent back toward $110
calls.note: No confirmation from either government, and no fresh denial either. Brent still climbed back toward $110 overnight, on tanker attacks spreading to the Gulf of Oman rather than on the talks.

calls.text: RBA's Hauser 5:30 PM CT: leaning on sticky inflation keeps a November hike near 1 in 3; leaning on the softer job market trims it
calls.note: Hauser leaned on sticky inflation: the outlook is 'materially worse'. Odds of a November hike rose to about 40% from about 30%, and the Aussie hit a three-week high near 0.702.

calls.text: China Q3 GDP 4.5% vs 4.4% fc — the aussie's demand read
calls.note: Beat: 4.5% vs 4.4% fc (q/q 1.2%); retail +1.1% the standout. AUD/USD +0.3-0.5% to ~0.697, the night's best G10 performer; USD/CNH 6.6811, strongest since June 2022. Two-speed beat (factories lead, property -20.6% YTD).

calls.text: Petersburg Oil Terminal drone strike — Baltic supply risk into Monday's open vs the waiver's lower-price pull
calls.note: Fire CONFIRMED (Beglov; Fire Point confirmed its FP-1 hit the terminal); ~1 killed, several injured (figures vary); damage extent still unquantified. Crude's Sunday open came flat — neither the spike nor the tumble; Asia Brent -1.0 to -1.8%.

calls.text: Beirut strike fallout: the haven-bid tell at Monday's open
calls.note: No Hezbollah retaliation as of Monday's open (Qmati: strike crossed a 'red line', leadership to decide; IDF: normal routines). Haven bid stayed sheathed — DXY flat 101.80-101.83, havens ~flat in Asia. The tell held: no escalation, no haven extension.

calls.text: October FOMC priced as a hold (~85%) into the Saturday blackout; December is the live debate
Brent broke $108 on Ukraine refinery strikes — $105-112 range into the weekend (prior $104-108 call broken)
USD/CAD holds 1.41-1.43 into the BoC (Oct 28); Canada CPI Mon the trigger
calls.note: Oct 19: CPI passed without a break — USD/CAD ~1.411 at the NY close, still inside the range. Runs to the Oct 28 decision. Oct 20: dipped to ~1.409, a hair under the floor, as oil and BoC hike bets lifted the loonie. Oct 20 close: broke below the floor — USD/CAD ~1.406, strongest loonie since Sep 22, on BoC hike pricing (~80–85%) and Alberta's vote to remain.
The tripwire never bit — Friday's waiver suspends the duties outright with no end date. Superseded by the ~Dec 17 60-day review clock.
calls.text: Graham Act Oct-18 tripwire: waivers extended or enforcement begins — oil's Sunday open is the tell
Iran deal Sunday signing: Trump's 'OPEN TO ALL' vs Tehran's 'not tomorrow' — the strait itself is the verdict
calls.note: No signed deal carried by any major wire by 4pm CT Sunday; Trump's 'complete' claim stands unverified against Tehran's 'talks stalled'. Aggregator 'markets celebrate' content held — its futures numbers contradict Friday's verified settles. The signing test is claim day, not done day.

calls.text: Canada CPI Mon 7:30am CT (TD 3.2%, UBS 3.3%, RBC 3.0%): hot (3.3%+) revives the Oct 28 hike; soft (3.0%-) buries it to December
calls.note: Neither branch: 3.1% vs 3.2% expected, core measures cooled to 1.8–1.9%. October stayed about 1 in 4 (a hold), with about one quarter-point hike priced by December; consumers' inflation expectations rose to ~3.9% in the BoC survey. Correction (Oct 20): by Monday's close swaps had jumped to ~87% for an October hike on Macklem's Saturday forecast warning; the 1-in-4 figure was stale.

calls.text: UK CPI Wed 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%): 3.5%+ starts pricing a December follow-up; soft reopens Bailey's 2027 read
calls.note: Hot branch: 3.5% vs 3.4% expected (3.1% in August), the highest in 11 months. November's hike is near certain; how much December moved was not yet verified at write.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (ANZ 3.8% y/y): hot settles the RBNZ's two-way bet toward the hike side
calls.note: Not hot: inflation came in at 3.7%, a touch soft. The hike side still settled anyway, with October 28 now about 98% priced.

calls.text: Japan CPI Fri + BoJ Oct 29-30: Ueda's 'quite close' language tested — October hike stays ~25%
calls.note: Oct 19: swaps now put an October 30 hike under 5% (BBH), below the ~25% in the call. December ~80% unchanged. October hike odds fell to about 4%, far below the ~25% in the call; Japan's inflation came in at 2.1% as expected and December (~80%) is now the meeting that matters.

calls.text: France's revenue-section budget vote Tue: a clean pass narrows the French–German spread (~141bp); a defeat or big concessions widens it and weighs on the euro
calls.note: No vote on Tuesday: it was pushed to October 27, so neither branch played out.

calls.text: UK jobs Tue 1 AM CT (earnings ~3.8% expected): sticky pay firms the BoE hike case before Wednesday's inflation; cooling pay backs Bailey's calmer view
calls.note: Sticky side won: unemployment fell to 4.7% (4.9% expected) and regular pay rose 3.7% (3.6% expected); total pay and claims were softer. Pound +0.3% to ~1.334.

calls.text: Konarak follow-through: a US confirmation or more strikes keeps oil's supply premium and lifts US yields; silence lets the morning's waiver drop resume
calls.note: No confirmation (a US official denied the strike) and no new strike overnight, yet the premium held: Brent ~$109.8 Tuesday on low Gulf flows and Iran's Hormuz claims. The waiver-driven drop did not resume.

calls.text: BoC Oct 28 with ~87% priced for a hike: a hike is mostly in the loonie already; a hold would be the surprise and hit it
calls.note: The Bank of Canada hiked as priced, and the loonie barely moved on the day.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (~3.8% y/y): near forecast keeps the ~80% hike pricing; clearly soft reopens the hold and weighs on the kiwi
calls.note: Near forecast (3.7% vs 3.8%) and hike pricing held, rising to about 98%; the kiwi dipped only briefly.
